subject: Agriculture
title: More Than Dirt
description: Learn More Than Dirt in one minute.

hook.text: People call it dirt. Scientists call it one of the most complex ecosystems on Earth.

buildup.text: Soil is a mix of minerals, organic matter, water, air, and billions of living organisms per handful.

discovery.text: It takes about 500 years to form one inch of topsoil. Nature builds it grain by grain.

twist.text: Erosion can strip that inch away in a single heavy rainstorm if the ground is left bare.

climax.text: 95% of our food comes from soil. Lose it, and farms fail. Civilizations have collapsed over less.

quiz.question: How long does it take to form one inch of topsoil naturally?

details.summary: Soil is a living ecosystem containing minerals, organic matter, water, air, and billions of organisms per handful. This topic introduces why soil is far more complex and important than the 'dirt' most people dismiss it as, and why understanding soil is essential for agriculture.
details.whyItMatters: Soil is the foundation of terrestrial life—95% of the world's food comes from soil. A single teaspoon contains more microorganisms than there are people on Earth, yet most people understand very little about this critical resource.
takeaways: Soil contains minerals, organic matter, water, air, and billions of living organisms
A teaspoon of healthy soil holds more microorganisms than people on Earth
It takes 500-1,000 years to form just one inch of topsoil naturally

faq.question: What makes soil different from plain dirt or rock dust?
faq.answer: Soil is a living system. Unlike inert crushed rock, soil contains organic matter from decomposed plants and animals, a vast community of bacteria, fungi, and invertebrates, pore spaces filled with air and water, and mineral nutrients in forms plants can absorb.

faq.question: Why is soil considered one of Earth's most important resources?
faq.answer: Soil produces 95% of global food, filters and stores fresh water, decomposes waste and recycles nutrients, stores more carbon than all plants and the atmosphere combined, and provides the foundation for terrestrial ecosystems. Without healthy soil, civilization cannot survive.
